claim.text: Daily reflective journaling improves writing self-efficacy in first-year students

papers.title: Structured reflection journals and writing confidence in first-year seminars

decision.label: supports
decision.rationale: The intervention group reported higher post-course self-efficacy than the comparison group.

excerpts.text: Mean writing self-efficacy increased more for students assigned to weekly guided reflection journals.

papers.title: Optional journaling and writing confidence in introductory composition

decision.label: does not support
decision.rationale: The optional journaling condition did not differ from the no-journal comparison on the self-efficacy scale.

excerpts.text: Optional journal completion was not associated with a statistically reliable self-efficacy gain.

papers.title: Guided reflective writing as a confidence scaffold for novice academic writers

decision.label: supports with caveats
decision.rationale: The guided reflection arm improved confidence, but only when instructors supplied weekly prompts.

excerpts.text: Prompted reflection produced a moderate gain in academic writing self-efficacy by the final week.
